text: Configuration is built, data is migrating cleanly. Chapter four proves it all actually works. This lesson covers the plan that governs testing and the test script, the artifact every subsequent testing lesson depends on.

A test plan defines, before any testing begins, the scope of modules and processes, the levels of testing that will happen, the environments each level runs in, who's responsible for writing and executing scripts, and the entry and exit criteria for each level. Without it, testing tends to happen ad hoc with no shared definition of done.

A test script is a specific, repeatable scenario: numbered steps, an expected result at each step or at the end, the actual result recorded by the person running it, and a pass or fail outcome. Good scripts are specific enough that someone unfamiliar with the requirement could run them and get a meaningful result.

Every test script should trace to one or more requirement IDs in the Requirements Traceability Matrix. That's what actually closes the loop the RTM was built for: a requirement now has a script proving it works. A requirement with no script, flagged back in lesson four as a red flag, gets caught here, before testing begins.

Brightfield's functional consultant writes test script CM-TS-07, tracing to requirement BR-CM-014: import a statement, verify it appears, confirm the auto-match rule reconciles it with no manual intervention. This script runs as-is in SIT and a close variant runs in UAT. Up next, lesson seventeen: System Integration Testing, where scripts actually get executed.
